## 维护者速读

- 问题:在按组织隔离数据的部署里,用"关联记录的条件"做筛选时,如果一张表归各组织、另一张是全平台共用(比如共用目录),匹配的关联记录超过一千条,整条查询明确报错;按共用表的字段做统计分组则直接被拒。碰到的是做跨表筛选和报表的人;自带应用里今天没有一处会撞到。
- 选项:A 把"关联表按哪个组织隔离"写进平台与数据库驱动的正式约定,上限取消、分组可用,约 3 个 PR(先改设计记录);B 走约定之外的旁路,约 2 个 PR,驱动漏接时会静默读到别的组织的数据;C 只放开"组织表查共用表"这一半,1 个 PR;D 维持现状,不动代码。
- 推荐 A,不加急:每张表各守各的组织边界才是长远形态,而且驱动漏接时是报错、不是泄露。今天没有实际需求,可以排在有人撞到之后。
- 不定会怎样:现状不变,超过一千条继续明确报错,不丢数据、不串组织;这张卡停在待裁,已收工的那次跨表筛选改造留一个"部分未达"的尾巴。

## Analysis

**One-sentence problem.** Under an organization wall, a filter or a report dimension that crosses from an organization's own table to a table shared by the whole platform (or back) does not get the uncapped one-statement read that same-kind tables got on 2026-11-16: the filter is refused past 1,000 related matches, and the report dimension is refused at any size.

**Background.** PR #33652 (merged 2026-11-16) serves a single-valued relation condition as one in-database subquery, "where it is provably the same read as the id read". Its contract review (record 6900638852, finding S3, should-fix) said: "Name a carrier, or ask for a ruling that the cap stays there." The seat `domain:server#5` chose to name a carrier and filed this card.

**Standing of the premise.** ⚠️ This card rests on a **seat ruling** (option B on PR #33652, contract finding S3), **not a maintainer ruling**. The maintainer-directed parent is #33626 (filing gate ③, 「首先保sql,应该用最高性能的方案」), whose item 2 reads "each hop carries that object's read scope and tenant wall". No maintainer record names this tenancy-class case. The accepted ADR text below conflicts with every option except D, so A, B and C are protocol changes, not a `Bug` fix (SKILL 〈升级与决策〉: 「改协议、新增公开面另立卡,⛔ 不作 Bug 选项」). The tenant wall is a security boundary, so this sits on the human floor whatever the letter.

Governing text: ADR-0139 D2 step 3, verbatim: "The composed leaf carries `{ object: P, scope }`. **The tenant wall is not composed here**: the driver applies its own tenant scope to the subquery's table with the outer read's options (D3). The engine never re-derives it." D3, `driver-sql` bullet, verbatim: "compiles the composed leaf in its filter compiler … to `field IN (SELECT id FROM P_TABLE WHERE SCOPE AND TENANT)`, the subquery scoped by `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts#applyTenantScope` with the outer read's options." The spec docblock on `ComposedReadableIds` repeats it. Re-check: `git show origin/main:docs/adr/0139-engine-internal-semi-join-leaf-readable-parent-ids.md | sed -n 191,206p`.

**Protocol change?** A: yes, the spec leaf shape, ADR-0139 D2/D3 and probably one driver-facing brand or declaration. B: yes, ADR-0139 D2/D3 plus a new `@objectstack/core` export that no spec type names. C: yes, ADR text only (direction 1 no longer "outer read's options" by proof, direction 2 unchanged). D: none.

- Relations from an organization-scoped object to a platform-global one (direction 1): **0**. Repo-wide lookups to either global object: **0**.
- Relations from a platform-global object to one the predicate classes as tenant-scoped (direction 2): **3** (`sys_api_key.user_id` and `sys_sso_provider.user_id` to `sys_user`, `sys_api_key.active_organization_id` to `sys_organization`). Both targets are `managedBy: 'better-auth'` and declare no organization column, so the wall is inert on them (inferred from the declarations, not from a running schema).
- Control: **90** of 94 relations are organization-to-organization and are served uncapped by #33652. The downstream pull that opened #33626 (a margin dashboard) is of this same-class kind.
- Reaching 1,000: only by filtering API keys or SSO providers on a user attribute that matches more than 1,000 users. No first-party view or filter spells such a path (`git grep -n -E "['\"](user_id|active_organization_id)\.[a-z_]+['\"]" origin/main -- packages/platform-objects/src examples` → 0). No example sets a walled posture. **Reading: zero measured pull today; reachable only in a large walled deployment through an author-written filter.**

**Questions.** Q1: which carrier, if any, takes the related table's own organization scope to the database subquery (A–D). Q2: who lands the ADR-0139 amendment (A/B). Q3: is the analytics dimension across tenancy classes in scope (A/B).

Nearest precedents: #34565 (a spec-declared driver fact with its engine readers and the ADR note, +726/−100, 36 files) and #33652 (the semi-join with SQLite and PG pins, +1623/−223, 27 files). No precedent for changing this leaf's shape |
| Q1 B, side table in core | An identity-keyed side table written by the engine, read by the drivers | Same when everything is current; on a duplicated core copy or an unaware driver, direction 2 reads the related table across every organization, silently | `domain:server` · ADR PR + 1 code PR over objectql, core, driver-sql, driver-turso. **No precedent** for an engine-to-driver fact outside spec |
| Q1 C, direction 1 only | Lift the gate where the related table is platform-global; keep the cap the other way | Shared-catalog filters uncapped; global-to-organization stays capped; the card stays half open | `domain:server` · 1 PR, objectql only. **No precedent** for a one-direction serve; the equality rests on a driver fact the engine does not own (P8, inferred) |
| Q1 D, keep the cap | Nothing changes | Past 1,000 a loud 400 that names the two-step route; never truncated | 0 PRs; the card closes as not planned. A to D differ by far more than 3× |
| Q2 A / B | A: a docs-only amendment PR first. B: the code PR carries it | None | A precedent: #33992 (+43/−0, 2 files, "This amendment declares; #33696's change lands only after it merges"). B precedent: #34565 (27 ADR lines inside a 36-file code PR) |

B: it stays refused at any size | A: one more compile site and pin pair inside Q1's PR, no separate precedent. B: no precedent (a second predicate over the same registry fact) |

**Business meaning.** A: every table checks its own organization badge at its own door, and that rule is written into the contract. B: the badge travels on a sticky note beside the contract, and if the note falls off, the door stays open. C: we open the shared-catalog door and leave the other one as it is. D: the reception desk keeps saying "too many matches, ask in two steps".

**Four axes, argued from the business side.**

- ① Long-term soundness. Two years on, a customer running many organizations on one database expects a shared catalog and per-organization data to filter and group together with no size limit, each table walled by its own organization. This is how PostgreSQL row-level security behaves (a policy belongs to the table and applies wherever that table is read, a subquery included). A reaches that state inside the one contract every driver already reads, and removes a special case (one hop class behaves differently) at the cost of one optional field. B reaches it with a second dialect beside the contract. C leaves a half. D keeps the special case and adds nothing. Reading: A.
- ② Real pull. Zero measured in first-party apps (0 direction-1 relations, 3 direction-2 relations into identity tables with no organization column, 0 filters through them). The downstream dashboard that drove #33626 is already served. Reading: defer or D.
- ③ AI-mistake resistance. Direction 2 is where a mistake is expensive. If a driver ignores the carried scope there, the related table is read with no organization filter, so **a user of organization B gets rows selected by related records that belong to organization A: a cross-organization read, with a normal 200 and no error**. Under A with a distinct brand, a driver that does not know the new leaf refuses (`INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500, the ADR-0139 D3 envelope): loud, an operator sees it, nobody sees foreign data. Under B the fallback to the outer options is silent by construction. C avoids direction 2 entirely. D is loud today (400). Reading: A with the refusing brand, or D; never B.
- ④ Start-up focus. A adds a permanent spec field and an obligation on every third-party driver that declares the leaf. D adds nothing and no gate. Reading: D.

os-decision-facets
① Long-term: A shrinks a behavioural special case and keeps one contract; B adds a second dialect; C is a half; D keeps the special case. No SQL slowdown for memory/Mongo parity in any option.
② Pull: zero first-party pull (0 / 3 / 0 as counted above; 90 of 94 relations already served); default defer or remove.
③ AI mistakes: A with a refusing brand fails loud (500); B fails silent into a cross-organization read; D is loud (400).
④ No proliferation: A is one more declared key held forever; D declares nothing.
Prior rulings read: "tenancy class" ReadableIds → 3 hits (#34157, #33626, #33619); ADR-0139 D2 step 3 / D3; thread: 4 (this card), plus PR #33652 records 6900638852 and 6902361654

**Recommendation.** Q1 **A**, with its sub-choice ruled in the same stroke: the leaf that carries a scope is a distinct brand that an unaware driver refuses (not a change to what the existing capability bit promises).
